title: Book Three · Chapter 175: The Triangle on the Desk
story:
Anna's receipt letter arrives the following week.

The design school has her form and all four drawing copies. It will review them in winter and send a decision in spring.

Anna shows Ronan the letter before her after-school maths group.

“All the baskets arrived,” she says.

“And the shutter?”

“Still half closed.”

He laughs and gives the page back. She puts it in her own folder, then takes a piece of paper from her book.

Today she is helping a few younger students with their teacher. Ronan has work to finish in the library. They will meet afterward.

When he returns, the group is still around a desk. Anna has drawn a large triangle on her paper.

The left and right sides have the same length. She marks them with short pencil lines.

“Which corners match?” she asks.

A girl points to the two lower corners.

“How can we check?”

The girl looks at the shape for a while. Another student suggests a ruler.

Anna folds the paper down the middle. The two marked sides meet. The lower corners lie together too.

The girl leans closer and puts a finger beside the fold.

“There.”

Anna opens the paper again and asks her to explain it.

The girl begins with one finger on the lower corner.

“This one goes there.”

Anna lets her finish. Then she puts her own hand beside the other corner.

“Can you say which corner?”

The girl looks at the two little marks on the sides. She moves her finger up one side, then down the other.

She starts again, more slowly.

The other student keeps the paper still. Nobody folds it for her this time.

Ronan can see the girl find the words as she follows the pencil lines. Anna listens and follows the girl's finger.

When the girl stops, Anna points to the matched side marks once more. The girl nods and finishes the last part herself.

The paper is a little soft along the fold now. It is still clear enough for the others to see. Ronan stays by the door and leaves the space around the desk to the group. This time, the girl uses the pencil marks and the fold in her answer.

The teacher comes over to listen. Anna moves aside so the girl can show the paper herself.

Ronan waits by the door. He watches Anna listen, then smile at one part of the explanation.

At last, the younger students put their books away. Anna takes the folded triangle and her folder from the desk.

Outside, Ronan asks about the group.

“I help some afternoons,” she says. “The teacher chooses the questions.”

“They liked the paper.”

“It is easier to see than my first drawing.”

She shows him the thick pencil line she rubbed out. There is still a grey mark across one corner.

Ronan opens his bag and finds a little space for her folded paper while she ties her shoe. He gives it back when she stands.

“A whole school in that folder,” he says.

“And one fruit shop.”

They walk to the gate together. Lin is waiting near the road, so Anna stops to tell her about the girl's answer.

Ronan hears the two of them start another maths question. He lifts a hand and takes his own road home, with the sound of Anna's laugh behind him.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

triangle＝三角形；fold＝折叠、折线；match＝相合、对应；suggest＝提出一个办法。

## 理解问题

1. Anna的收件信是否意味着录取？哪些材料已收到？
2. 她怎样让年轻同学看懂三角形？Ronan是否替她完成或领导这个学习小组？

## 读句子

**The two marked sides meet.**

拆开看：The two marked sides / meet.

标了记号的两条边／折到一起重合了。
